s1.syndrome_frame: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema on the face with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema below the left lower eyelid
Granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin
No evidence of malignancy or infection
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
Several-month history of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema
Location: below the left lower eyelid
History of chronic scleritis treated with NSAIDs
Left levator resection for ptosis
Dacryocystorhinostomy one month before the onset of the lesion
Two courses of antibiotics for presumed postoperative cellulitis
CT scan showed soft-tissue thickening of the anterior-inferior orbital rim and lower eyelid
No extension into surrounding structures or bony invasion
Excisional biopsy performed
Intraoperative frozen sections revealed granulomatous inflammation
Final histopathology showed granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin
No evidence of malignancy or infection

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology shows granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive mucin, consistent with granuloma annulare

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Although not all defining features are present, the presence of granulomatous inflammation and mucin makes it a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Periocular xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Location and histopathology are consistent with this diagnosis, which is a type of non-X histiocytosis

shortlist.label: Foreign body granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Recent surgical history and presence of granulomatous inflammation raise the possibility of a foreign body reaction

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation is a hallmark of sarcoidosis, although other features such as lung involvement are not mentioned in the case context

raw.rationale: The presence of granulomatous inflammation with central necrobiosis and extensive Alcian-Blue positive mucin in the histopathology is consistent with Granuloma annulare, and the clinical presentation of a painless, firm area of induration and mild erythema also supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Periocular xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: No mention of xanthomatous features or lipid deposits in the histopathology

rejected.label: Foreign body granuloma
rejected.why: No history of foreign body exposure or evidence of foreign material in the histopathology

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: No systemic symptoms or other organ involvement suggestive of sarcoidosis
